note: the last position the expedition itself recorded: the ships deserted, beset since 12 September 1846 at lat 70 deg 05' N long 98 deg 23' W
INFERRED, not testimony: the drift south along the west coast of King William Island that the Inuit accounts require. No informant gave a position here

testimony of Kok-lee-arng-nun and his wife to Hall, April 1866: the ship they had often seen Too-loo-ark (Franklin) aboard was crushed by heavy ice in the spring, turned on her side, holed and sank at once with several men still in her. They gave no position; the bay is Terror Bay, where the wreck of HMS Terror was found in 2016

testimony of In-nook-poo-zhee-jook to Hall, 1869, pointing on McClintock's chart: the other ship, three masts and four boats at the davits, all in complete order, beset in ice of one winter's make off Ook-joo-lik (Utjulik) near O'Reilly Island. Hall gives lat 68 deg 30' N long 99 deg W, early in the spring of 1849

testimony of Ikinnelikpatolok to Schwatka's party, 1879: the ship frozen in near an island about five miles due west of Grant Point; a dead man in a bunk; his people cut a hole in her side at the level of the ice and she filled and sank when the ice broke up the following summer. The wreck of HMS Erebus was found here on 2 September 2014
